evals.prompt: I'm designing the refund state machine for our marketplace (requested → approved → partially_refunded → refunded, plus disputes from the card network that can arrive at any point). I'm not sure it handles a dispute arriving after a partial refund. Can you prototype it so I can poke at it? Repo is TypeScript with pnpm.
evals.expected_output: Chooses the logic branch: a tiny interactive terminal app around a pure, portable state machine/reducer, runnable with one pnpm command, in-memory, printing full state after every action.
expectations: Picks the logic branch (interactive terminal app), not a UI prototype
States the question being prototyped explicitly at the top of the file or in a README before writing code
Isolates the logic in a pure, portable module (reducer or explicit state machine) with no I/O, separate from the throwaway TUI
Makes it runnable with one command via the project's existing tooling (e.g. a pnpm script) and keeps state in memory with no persistence
Prints the full state after every action

evals.prompt: Prototype a few options for how the new 'Usage & limits' section should look on our existing /settings/billing page in our Next.js app. Not sure if it should be a table, progress bars, or something else.
evals.expected_output: Chooses the UI branch, sub-shape A: several radically different variants on the existing /settings/billing route switched by ?variant= and a floating bottom bar.
expectations: Picks the UI branch (several radically different variations), not a logic prototype
Uses sub-shape A: renders variants inside the existing /settings/billing page rather than creating a new standalone route
Switches variants via a ?variant= URL search param and a floating bottom bar
Defaults to around 3 variants (capped at 5) that are radically different from one another
Skips polish: no tests, no abstractions, and marks the code clearly as a prototype

evals.prompt: Quick prototype: does an append-only ledger model for loyalty points (earn, redeem, expire, reverse) let us compute a correct balance when an earn is reversed after some of those points were already redeemed? Python project, uses uv.
evals.expected_output: Logic branch in Python via uv, pure ledger functions, in-memory, state surfaced after each action, and a plan to capture the verdict and prototype on a throwaway branch afterwards.
expectations: Picks the logic branch and uses Python run via the project's existing tooling (e.g. `uv run <path>`) as a single command
Implements the ledger as pure functions or a reducer over a plain data type, with the TUI importing it rather than the reverse
Keeps state in memory (no database) and prints the full ledger and balance after each action
Plans to capture the prototype on a throwaway branch out of main and record the verdict and the question it settled in the issue or a commit
